name: Regression Bisection Common Pitfalls

content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday regression bisection work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical regression bisection tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Measure before optimizing any regression bisection bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
2. Keep regression bisection changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. When multiple regression bisection strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. When regression bisection guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Prefer the simplest regression bisection approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to regression bisection (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Keep regression bisection outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. Document any non-obvious regression bisection decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen regression bisection approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting regression bisection assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new regression bisection abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop regression bisection edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about regression bisection over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
